name: add-key-nonallowlisted
why: a single add_key() from a process outside the keyring allowlist is the anchor the rule fires on
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for keyring_stuffing_behavioral.c's add_key() record

name: add-key-burst
why: a rapid burst of add_key() from one non-allowlisted pid (the keyring-stuffing primitive); each call independently satisfies the rule
source: synthetic: keyring_stuffing_behavioral.c run with a count, three of its add_key records

name: keyctl-not-add-key
why: keyctl() reads/updates existing keys and is far more common than add_key; it keeps the keyring-syscall surface, so the syscall==add_key anchor must be load-bearing (the atomic itself issues keyctl for cleanup)
source: synthetic: keyctl(KEYCTL_CLEAR) cleanup from a non-allowlisted process

name: request-key-not-add-key
why: request_key() looks up a key and upcalls to create one via the kernel, a benign keyring operation; same surface, different syscall, so it must not fire

name: gnome-keyring-allowlisted
why: gnome-keyring-daemon adds keys constantly; the comm allowlist alone must suppress it

name: gssproxy-allowlisted
why: gssproxy installs Kerberos credentials into the keyring; the allowlisted GSSAPI identity must be filtered

name: unrelated-write
why: an ordinary write(): a sanity floor that proves the add_key selection does not fire on noise
